reader.requirement: At --std 85, MULTIPLY format 2 must multiply literal-1 / identifier-1 by literal-2 / identifier-2 once and store that product into each identifier-3 (numeric or numeric edited) in turn, each with its own ROUNDED, an identifier-3 that is also an operand not changing the product stored into later ones.

reader.notes: The product is rendered per receiver at its own scale and ROUNDED mode from operands identified once, which equals one product rounded into each receiver. The 1985 composite is the receiving items only, capped at 18, as CheckComposite's 85 arm implements.

refuter.evidence: rmul1.cob at --std 85 (rmul1-001): MULTIPLY 25 BY 6 GIVING P1 ROUNDED P2 (PIC 9PP) gives N2=200 100 (rounding at the rightmost allocated integer position, §1985:VI.6.4.1); MULTIPLY F BY 5 GIVING NR ROUNDED NT with F=-0.5 gives N3=-3 -2 (absolute value increased); 10 BY 10 GIVING BN PIC 99 COMP takes the size error, BN unchanged N4 SIZE 00 (largest value is the PICTURE's, §1985:VI.6.4.2(3)); 20 BY 5 GIVING ED (Z9) ED2 (99) both unchanged N6 SIZE [ 7] 07. rmul2.cob --compile-only: GIVING a Z(17)9.99 receiver refused COBOL0805 composite 20 digits (and COBOL0802 for the item itself). cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.20.4 GR2 'the result is stored in the data items referenced by each identifier-3'; OK §1985:VI.6.4.1 'rounding or truncation occurs relative to the rightmost integer position for which storage is allocated'; OK §1985:VI.6.4.2 'the maximum value implied by the associated decimal PICTURE character-string'.
